findings.comment: No building elevation drawings are included in the bound plan set (39 sheets). Building height information is provided only in tabular form on Sheet 9 (Building Height Table) and Sheet 29 (Finished Floor Elevations). Architectural elevation sheets must be included in the bound plan set and referenced in the Index of Sheets.

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the 8 buildings. No elevation views are shown for any sides of any building. Provide separate architectural elevation sheets for each of the 8 distinct building types, showing all visible elevations from cardinal directions.

The project includes multiple distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex) as shown in the Building Data Table on Sheet 9, but no separate architectural elevation sheets are provided for each building type. Provide distinct elevation sheets for each building type.

Building heights are shown in feet on the site plan data table (Sheet 9), but elevation sheets—which are the primary location for detailed height labeling—are not provided. Provide building elevation sheets with heights clearly labeled in feet from the average adjacent grade to the applicable roof point.

Building height is not labeled in number of stories on elevation sheets. While Sheet 9 notes 'Maximum Number of Building Stories = 3,' individual story counts are not labeled for each of the 8 buildings. Provide elevation sheets labeling the number of stories for each building.

Heights of individual buildings are shown in the Site Plan data table (Sheet 9) ranging from 33'-4.75" to 36'-1", with maximum height of 36'-1" (Building 3) identified, but no elevation sheets are provided where heights would be clearly separated by building. Provide architectural elevation sheets showing heights for each individual building.

Elevation sheets do not show the average adjacent grade (AAG) calculation. While the Building Height Table on Sheet 9 lists an 'Average (MSL)' value for each building (e.g., 686.25, 684.50, 685.00, etc.), it does not identify the highest and lowest grade points at the building perimeter or show the AAG calculation formula AAG = (highest + lowest) ÷ 2. The Grading Plan (Sheet 11) contains numerous spot elevations around buildings but lacks labeled AAG values and dimension lines from AAG to the roof point. Provide elevation sheets showing the highest and lowest grade points at each building perimeter (labeled 'AT BUILDING PERIMETER') and the vertical dimension from the calculated AAG to the applicable measurement point.

The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 does not specify the roof type for each building (flat, pitched, hip, mansard, or other), which is required to determine the correct height measurement methodology per LDC § 25-1-21(50). Different roof types require measurement to different points: flat roofs measure to the top of coping; pitched or hip roofs measure to the average height of the highest gable; mansard roofs measure to the deck line; other styles measure to the highest point. Provide elevation sheets identifying the roof type for each building and documenting that the correct measurement point was used for each roof type.

Building height values show discrepancies across plan documents. The Building Height Table on Sheet 9 shows 'Average (MSL)' values (e.g., Building 1: 686.25, Building 2: 684.50) that differ from the Finished Floor Elevations shown on Sheet 11 Grading Plan and Sheet 29 Addressing Plan (e.g., Building 1: FFE 687.50, Building 2: FFE 685.50). The difference between 'Average (MSL)' and FFE is not explained, creating confusion about which value represents the grade baseline for height measurement. Ensure all height values are consistent across elevation sheets, site plan data tables, grading plan, addressing plan, and project narrative, and reconcile any differences with clear notation of whether values represent AAG, FFE, or finished grade at specific locations.
